name: AngularJS
summary: Google's first-generation framework — end-of-life since 2021, and not the same product as Angular.
what_it_is: A framework built around two-way data binding, directives that extend HTML, dependency injection and scopes. It reached end of long-term support in January 2022 and receives no further patches, including security patches.
why_it_matters: AngularJS is the sharpest illustration of why this archive needed rebuilding. It sat in the original 2021 frontend list presented as a current recommendation, years after it was superseded and shortly before support ended entirely — because the old data model was append-only and nothing could ever be removed. It is kept here, marked legacy, as the worked example of the failure being corrected. Its practical value now is diagnostic: recognising ng-* attributes dates a codebase precisely.
suitable_for: Maintaining or assessing existing AngularJS applications ahead of migration
Recognising the framework when you inherit it
not_suitable_for: Any application handling sensitive data — it receives no security patches
Teams expecting the knowledge to transfer to modern Angular, which is a different framework
verifiable_facts: The project's own support-status page records that long-term support ended; it receives no further patches.
editorial_interpretation: That its remaining value is diagnostic — recognising it dates a codebase.
context_dependent_guidance: Suitable: Maintaining or assessing existing AngularJS applications ahead of migration
Suitable: Recognising the framework when you inherit it
Unsuitable: Any application handling sensitive data — it receives no security patches
Unsuitable: Teams expecting the knowledge to transfer to modern Angular, which is a different framework
evidence_gaps: None material. This is the best-evidenced record in the set.
wrong_if: The cited support-status page is superseded or its date is misread.
signal_note: Repository signals are recorded file changes. They are not evidence of popularity, personal usage or industry trends, and none is eligible to inform a trend conclusion.
proposed_decision: Approve lifecycle "legacy" and the 2 dependent rule(s), or amend.
